_readme: 'constant' answers one question per entry: this column or branch holds
nothing in every row we publish -- is that the game, or is that us? An
entry here is the written claim that somebody checked the RAW capture,
not the merged store, because the merge is the thing under suspicion.
Adding a key to quiet a red line, without doing that, defeats the file.
'counts' is the row-count and list-length baseline. Growth is reported;
a drop is a failure. Re-record it with:  python tools/audit_columns.py --accept

constant.by-mode/*.tsv.gz:*: The .wdb-derived tables are decoded from fixed-width record structures, so every field in the layout becomes a column whether or not this client ever wrote anything into it -- 3.3.5 leaves whole blocks unused (unk1, Data11/16/17/21, questItem1-6, the em0_*/em1_* emote slots, BroadcastTextID*), and a mode with few submissions has more of them than a mode with many. 1,126 such columns, one reason, so this is a glob rather than 1,126 copies of a sentence. What makes that safe is that these files are the ONE part of the dataset with an independent proof of completeness: selftest.py checks every published record's payload byte-for-byte against the bytes a real client wrote for that entry, and checks that no submitted record went missing. A zero here is therefore the client's zero, not ours. It is also why the glob cannot hide a regression -- the per-column live-row count in 'counts' below is compared for every column regardless of this entry, so a column that ever carried data and stops is still a hard failure.
constant.catalogue/creatures.tsv:display_id: A capture gap, recoverable from a future NPC dump; see the creatures.tsv:type entry.
constant.catalogue/creatures.tsv:lock_id: NOT a gap, and deliberately worded differently from type/display_id above. A lock is a GameObject concept -- a door or a chest is locked, a creature is not -- so this column reaches creatures.tsv only because the two catalogues share one 19-column header. No future dump will ever fill it. If that shared header is ever split, these two entries go with it.
constant.catalogue/creatures.tsv:lock_type: NOT a gap; see the creatures.tsv:lock_id entry.
constant.catalogue/creatures.tsv:type: A CAPTURE GAP, and recoverable -- not the same thing as the two lock_ columns above, so do not fold all four together. creatures.tsv and gameobjects.tsv share one 19-column header (ingest_gameobjects.COLS) and the NPC dumper filled fewer of them. Checked at the source rather than in the merged table: across all five dumps-part1/dumps/dump_npc_<Zone>.txt the whole key set is exactly id, Name, 'Map internal name', MapX, MapY, 'internal map id' and 'internal X'/'Y'/'Z' -- nine keys, with 0 occurrences of type, displayid, lockid or locktype -- while the GameObject dumps (dumps_part2/dump_<Zone>.csv, semicolon CSV, header Id;Name;Type;DisplayId;...) yield 1,778 readable types and 1,774 display ids. But a creature genuinely HAS a type and a display id in the game; this dumper simply never wrote them. Same class as the skillCards *.cards entry: recovering it needs a new capture, not a decoder fix, and when one arrives this line should be deleted rather than reworded.
constant.lua/harvest/advancement.tsv:RequiredClas: Genuinely zero on both realms. The addon captured the field on every node -- grep counts 194,750 literal '["RequiredClassAEInvestment"] = 0' in the eleven raw .lua captures and not one other value, and the parser agrees at 389,500 node readings all zero. Ascension ships the gate and never uses it, on Darkmoon - Season 10 Wildcard or Dawnrise - Season 10 Freepick. Publishing the column is right: 'this gate exists and is always open' is itself preservation data, and a future capture from a realm that does use it will simply stop matching this line.
Identical to RequiredClassAEInvestment: 194,750 raw occurrences, every one zero. See that entry.
constant.lua/harvest/byRealm.json:*.apiSurfaces.s: The API-surface probe lists the members it can see on each global table. C_Timer came back with none: 17 raw occurrences, every one an empty table, 34 readings all length 0. Either the client exposes no enumerable members on C_Timer or the probe cannot see them. The empty entry is still worth publishing, because 'we asked and the answer was nothing' is a different statement from 'we never asked', and this file is the only place that distinction survives.
constant.lua/harvest/byRealm.json:*.skillCards.ty: A real gap in the capture, and worth saying so plainly rather than hiding it. The harvester recorded each skill-card TYPE (its name and its cost) but never enumerated the cards inside it: all 144 occurrences of '["cards"] = {' in the raw captures are followed immediately by '},', and the parser sees length 0 on all 36 readings of every one of the eight types. Nothing was lost in the merge -- there was never anything there. Recovering it needs a new capture from a client with the card list open.
constant.lua/harvest/byRealm.json:*.wildcard.elig: A probe result, not a table of game data -- it is what the API said about whichever character happened to be logged in when the addon ran. It came back empty every time: 11 raw occurrences, all empty, 22 readings all []. The interesting half of every probe is collected into observed.json instead, which is where an eventual non-empty answer will show up.
constant.lua/harvest/byRealm.json:*.wildcard.even: Empty on the events themselves, and that is correct: within events, startingChoice is [] in 59,714 readings and absent in the other 580, across all three realm buckets. The populated one lives a level up at wildcard.statics.startingChoice and it survived the merge -- Darkmoon - Season 10 Wildcard carries EntryID 36459 / SpellID 271205 (Rare, rank 1) and EntryID 42115 / SpellID 70152 among others. So this branch being empty is the shape of the data, not a loss; the check would still fire if the statics copy ever went empty too. The '*' covers all three buckets including '(unattributed)', which is where the three earliest captures go -- they predate byRealm and name no realm anywhere, so their advancement and wildcard trees are not guessed onto a real realm.
constant.lua/harvest/vendors.tsv:cost_count_2: Same fixed 6-slot array as cost_item_2; see that entry.
constant.lua/harvest/vendors.tsv:cost_count_3: Same fixed 6-slot array as cost_item_2; see that entry.
constant.lua/harvest/vendors.tsv:cost_item_2: GetMerchantItemCostInfo always returns a fixed SIX-slot cost array, so slots 2 and 3 exist for every row whether or not anything is in them. Across 7,582 item readings in the raw captures every single array is 6 long, and only slot 1 ever carries a currency -- it holds {n=3, texture, count, itemLink} while the other five are the empty {n=2, [2]=0}. So: no vendor item we have captured costs more than one currency. That is a fact about these 88 vendor pages, not a gap. It stops being true the moment somebody captures a vendor that charges two currencies at once, and this line should then be deleted rather than reworded.
constant.lua/harvest/vendors.tsv:cost_item_3: Same fixed 6-slot array as cost_item_2; see that entry.
